title: Dire non : pas, jamais, si et non plus
summary: Build present-tense negatives, change quantity articles when needed, and respond clearly to negative statements.
objectives: Place `ne/n'` and `pas/jamais` around the conjugated verb, including reflexives.
Use `de/d'` after negative quantities without changing definite articles or ordinary `être` identifications.
Use `si` to contradict a negative and `non plus` to share it.

sections.title: The two negative words surround the conjugated verb
paragraphs: For not, put `ne` before the conjugated verb and `pas` after it. `Ne` becomes `n'` before a vowel or silent `h`. Object and reflexive pronouns stay between `ne` and the verb: `je ne me lève pas`, `elle ne nous regarde pas`. In informal speech, `ne` is often omitted; recognise that usage, but keep it in these standard written tasks.

With a conjugated verb followed by an infinitive, the ordinary negative surrounds the conjugated verb: `je ne peux pas venir`. If only the infinitive is made negative, `ne pas` stays together before it: `je préfère ne pas venir`. These constructions need not mean the same thing.
points: Do not copy English don't as an extra French verb.
`Ne` + pronoun + conjugated verb + `pas` is the standard reflexive order.

examples.english: We do not go to bed early.
examples.note: The reflexive pronoun stays before the verb.

examples.english: I do not want to leave.

examples.note: Here the infinitive itself is negative.

mistakes.why: `Pas` follows the conjugated verb, not the infinitive.

sections.title: For 'none', an indefinite or partitive object normally takes `de`
paragraphs: After a negative expressing absence or zero quantity, `un`, `une`, `des`, `du`, `de la` and `de l'` normally become `de`, or `d'` before a vowel or silent `h`: `je n'ai pas de vélo`; `elle ne boit pas d'eau`. The noun still keeps its intended number: `pas de livre` or `pas de livres` depends on the context.

Keep definite `le/la/l'/les` when talking about an identified thing or a general category: `je n'aime pas le café`. After `être` in an ordinary identification, keep the original article: `ce n'est pas un musée`, `ce n'est pas du lait`. An explicit contrast can also preserve an indefinite article: `je n'ai pas un vélo, mais deux`. The zero-quantity rule is not an instruction to replace every article after any negative.
points: Ask whether the sentence denies a quantity, identifies something differently or names a specific/category object.

examples.french: J'ai une voiture. Je n'ai pas **de** voiture.
examples.english: I have a car. I do not have a car.
examples.note: `Une` becomes `de` when the quantity is zero.
`De l'` becomes `d'` in this ordinary negative quantity.
The definite article naming the category stays.

mistakes.why: For the intended ordinary meaning 'I have no keys', `des` becomes `de`.

sections.title: `Jamais` replaces `pas` to say never
paragraphs: `Ne… jamais` means never. `Jamais` occupies the usual position after the conjugated verb: `elle ne vient jamais`. In this basic construction, do not add `pas` as well. Reflexive pronouns remain in the same place before the verb. `Jamais` has other uses in questions and comparisons at later levels; here the target is a straightforward negative habit.
points: For never with an infinitive after a first verb: `je ne veux jamais conduire`.

sections.title: `Si` contradicts a negative; `non plus` shares it
paragraphs: Use `si`, rather than `oui`, to contradict a negative question or statement: `Tu ne viens pas ? — Si, je viens`. A reply `Non, je ne viens pas` confirms that you are not coming. `Non plus` means not either or neither when you share a negative fact: `moi non plus`, or `je ne viens pas non plus`. For a shared positive fact, use `aussi`, not `non plus`.
points: Listen to the negative wording before choosing `oui`, `non` or `si`.

examples.french: Tu n'as pas de billet ? — **Si**, j'ai un billet.
examples.english: Don't you have a ticket? — Yes, I do have a ticket.

examples.french: Je ne bois pas de café. — **Moi non plus**.
examples.english: I don't drink coffee. — Neither do I.

mistakes.prefer: Je ne viens pas non plus.
mistakes.why: For the intended meaning 'I am not coming either', use `non plus`.

sections.title: Move the negative only if you mean to change its scope
paragraphs: Compare the same action with two placements. `Vous ne pouvez pas participer` denies the possibility or permission to participate. `Vous pouvez ne pas participer` allows the option of not participating. With an infinitive alone, `ne pas` comes before it; if that infinitive is reflexive, its pronoun follows `ne pas`. Read the intended permission or choice first, then decide which verb the negative belongs to.

examples.french: Sans inscription, vous **ne pouvez pas participer**.
examples.english: Without registration, you cannot take part.

examples.french: La visite est facultative : vous **pouvez ne pas participer**.
examples.english: The visit is optional: you are allowed not to take part.
examples.note: Not participating is an available choice.

examples.french: Nous préférons **ne pas nous asseoir** près de la porte.
examples.english: We prefer not to sit down near the door.
examples.note: `Ne pas` precedes the reflexive pronoun and infinitive.

sections.title: A subject's identity is not an absent quantity
paragraphs: The article can remain when a negative tells us what a subject does not become or remain. In `ce bâtiment ne devient pas un hôtel`, `un hôtel` describes the building's proposed identity; it is not a quantity of hotels that someone lacks. This extends the meaning-based distinction behind `ce n'est pas un hôtel`. Ask whether the noun describes the subject or an amount denied, rather than memorising a ban on articles after `ne`.

examples.french: Cette salle **ne reste pas une réserve** : elle devient un atelier.
examples.english: This room does not remain a storeroom: it becomes a workshop.
examples.note: `Une réserve` (f.) here is a storeroom; `une` describes what the room remains.

examples.french: Ce jus **ne devient pas du vin** en une heure.
examples.english: This juice does not turn into wine in an hour.
examples.note: `Du vin` names the substance it does not become; this is not a statement that no wine is available.

examples.french: Nous **n'avons pas de vin** pour le dîner.
examples.english: We do not have any wine for dinner.
examples.note: Here the message really is zero available quantity, so `de` is appropriate.

practice.prompt: Signing is optional. Which sentence explicitly allows the choice not to sign?
practice.explanation: Pouvez allows the negative action ne pas signer. The other placement denies permission or ability to sign.

practice.prompt: Make only the infinitive reflexive action negative by inserting ne pas: 'Je préfère me lever maintenant.' Keep all other words.
answers: Je préfère ne pas me lever maintenant.
practice.explanation: Ne pas belongs before me lever, rather than surrounding préfère.

practice.prompt: Deny the possibility of entering by adding ne and pas around pouvoir: 'Nous pouvons entrer.'
practice.explanation: This denies entering; nous pouvons ne pas entrer would instead present not entering as a choice.

practice.prompt: Keep the subject's identity, rather than applying a zero-quantity rule: 'L'ancienne école ne devient pas ___ hôtel.' Choose un or de.
practice.explanation: Un hôtel says what the building does not become; it is not an absent object quantity.

practice.prompt: Choose une or de for the retained description: 'Cette cabane ne reste pas ___ simple remise.'
practice.explanation: Une simple remise describes the cabane after rester.

practice.prompt: Choose du or de when denying a transformation: 'Le lait ne devient pas ___ fromage en quelques secondes.'
practice.explanation: Du fromage identifies the resulting substance, rather than a quantity someone does not have.

practice.prompt: Make 'Je travaille.' negative with ne...pas. Write the whole sentence.
practice.explanation: Ne and pas surround the conjugated verb.

practice.prompt: Supply the zero-quantity article: 'Je n'ai pas ___ chien.'
practice.explanation: An indefinite object becomes de in this negative.

practice.prompt: Make 'Elle vient.' mean 'She never comes' using ne...jamais.
practice.explanation: Jamais replaces pas.

practice.prompt: You ARE coming. Answer 'Tu ne viens pas ?' with one word.
practice.explanation: Si contradicts the negative question.

practice.prompt: Make 'Il habite ici.' negative with ne...pas. Write the whole sentence.
practice.explanation: Ne elides before the silent h.

practice.prompt: Make 'Je me lève tôt.' negative with ne...pas. Write the whole sentence.
answers: Je ne me lève pas tôt.
practice.explanation: Ne precedes me; pas follows lève.

practice.prompt: Negate pouvons with ne...pas in 'Nous pouvons entrer.' Write the whole sentence.
practice.explanation: The conjugated verb is pouvons; the infinitive stays after pas.

practice.prompt: Supply the ordinary negative quantity form: 'Elle ne prend pas ___ soupe.'
practice.explanation: Partitive de la becomes de.

practice.prompt: Supply the ordinary negative quantity form: 'Nous n'avons pas ___ huile.'
practice.explanation: Use d' before the silent h and vowel.

practice.prompt: Keep the appropriate article: 'Ce n'est pas ___ vélo.' Choose un or de.
practice.explanation: An identification after être keeps the indefinite article.

practice.prompt: Make 'On se couche tard.' mean 'We never go to bed late', using ne...jamais.
answers: On ne se couche jamais tard.
practice.explanation: On takes the singular verb and se; jamais follows couche.

practice.prompt: Agree with 'Je n'aime pas ce film' using moi and the two-word negative addition.
practice.explanation: Moi non plus shares a negative opinion.

practice.prompt: Supply le or de: 'Je n'aime pas ___ fromage.'
practice.explanation: A category after aimer keeps its definite article under negation.

practice.prompt: You DO have a car. Supply one word: 'Tu n'as pas de voiture ? — ___, j'ai une voiture.'
practice.explanation: Si reverses the negative assumption.

practice.prompt: Make only the infinitive partir negative with ne pas: 'Je préfère partir.' Write the sentence.
practice.explanation: When negating the infinitive itself, ne pas stays together before it.

practice.prompt: Supply the ordinary zero-quantity form: 'Ils n'ont pas ___ billets.'
practice.explanation: Plural indefinite des becomes de.

practice.prompt: Make 'Je ne prends pas de sucre.' mean 'I do not take sugar either' by adding the negative addition at the end. Keep all the original words in order.
answers: Je ne prends pas de sucre non plus.
practice.explanation: Non plus at the end shares a negative habit. Aussi would express a positive addition.

production_task.prompt: Explain two things you do not do in your routine, one with `jamais` and one reflexive negative. Then respond to someone who shares one of those habits using `non plus`.
production_task.model_answer: Je ne bois jamais de café. Je ne me couche pas tard. Ma sœur ne boit pas de café non plus.
production_task.translation: I never drink coffee. I do not go to bed late. My sister does not drink coffee either.
rubric: Use `de` for a denied ordinary quantity.
Use `non plus` for a shared negative.
